messages:
deploy-bot: publish blocked for image: ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:v2026.03.01 due to provenance signature timestamp skew (signed_at=1700000000, now=1788881234) :warning:
maya: wait what, signed_at is in the past by a weird amount? how did that happen?
sam_engineer: seeing the same when I tried to mirror to ECR. CI job 4521 shows `provenance-verify` failing with `signature timestamp outside allowed window`. link: https://ci.redwood.internal/4521
leo_release: rolling window policy should tolerate skew up to +-2h. this looks like a day+, sounds like signer clock issue.
tara_sre: confirming: GCP builder VMs had an NTP outage this morning, some workloads drifted. authoring commit hash: 7f9a3b2. we need to decide rollback vs re-sign.
maya: can we re-sign the artifact without rebuilding? we want to avoid regenerating big model layers.
sam_engineer: re-sign is possible if we have the original build artifact and private key access. but our signing service rejects re-signs older than 24h by policy.
leo_release: options: 1) allow-list this signature as exception for this release window (manual override), 2) re-sign artifact after a short rebuild, or 3) promote a fallback image (v2026.03.01-compat) if available. preferences?
tara_sre: from SRE side, allow-list is fastest but increases risk surface. if we do allow-list, we should pin the image digest in the release notes and limit rollout percentage to 10% canary.
maya: fallback image exists but it's slightly older weights sharded-2026-02-25, quality regression unknown.
sam_engineer: quick check: we can re-run the signing step only if someone re-uploads the same blob to the registry. `s3 cp` + `sign-tool` should do it. it will take ~15m with upload time.
leo_release: timeline: we have a change window ending in 40m. recommend re-sign + canary if upload succeeds in 15-20m. if not, fall back to allow-list as emergency.
tara_sre: I'll prepare an allow-list PR but won't merge unless sign-tool fails. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/provenance/pull/189
sam_engineer: starting re-upload + sign now. command: ```
# mirror blob and sign
registryctl pull ghcr.io/redwood/runtime@sha256:abcd1234
registryctl push ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood/runtime:tmp-reupload
sign-tool sign --artifact tmp-reupload --kms key-prod --out signed-manifest.json
registryctl push-signed-manifest ecr... --manifest signed-manifest.json
```
maya: monitoring CI and deploybot.
deploy-bot: observed new signed manifest pushed to ecr.us-west-2 at 1788881295, running provenance verification...
deploy-bot: provenance verification PASSED for ghcr.io/redwood/runtime@sha256:abcd1234 (signed_at=1788881289) :white_check_mark:
leo_release: great. initiating canary rollout at 10% and pinning digest in release notes. please add a short note about the NTP incident.
tara_sre: added note and incident ticket: INC-2026-042. will follow up with builder fleet NTP fixes.
maya: thanks team. closing loop: no rollback required.
sam_engineer: leave the allow-list PR open but unmerged for audit trail.
leo_release: filing release note: "runtime: fixed provenance signature timestamp skew due to builder NTP drift; re-signed artifact and performed 10% canary. See INC-2026-042."
maya: :thumbsup:
